# Psalm 86 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Prayer of David. Incline your ear, O LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.

**2** Preserve my life, for I am godly; save your servant, who trusts in you — you are my God.

**3** Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to you do I cry all the day.

**4** Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.

**5** For you, O Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in steadfast love to all who call upon you.

**6** Give ear, O LORD, to my prayer; listen to my plea for grace.

**7** In the day of my trouble I call upon you, for you answer me.

**8** There is none like you among the gods, O Lord, nor are there any works like yours.

**9** All the nations you have made shall come and worship before you, O Lord, and shall glorify your name.

**10** For you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God.

**11** Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your truth; unite my heart to fear your name.

**12** I give thanks to you, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify your name forever.

**13** For great is your steadfast love toward me; you have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.

**14** O God, insolent men have risen up against me; a band of ruthless men seeks my life, and they do not set you before them.

**15** But you, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.

**16** Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your maidservant.

**17** Show me a sign of your favor, that those who hate me may see and be put to shame because you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 86.

- **86:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **86:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **86:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **86:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **86:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **86:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **86:11**: 'Unite my-heart' (yached levavi) — a prayer for inner coherence; the divided heart is the fundamental spiritual problem.
- **86:15**: Echoes Exodus 34:6 — the great self-revelation of YHWH's character: compassionate, gracious, slow-of-anger, abundant-in-chesed and emet.

### LOGOS
- **86:11**: 'Unite my heart to fear your name' — the petition for a unified heart (yached levavi) is unique in the Psalter. It recognizes that divided loyalties are the root of spiritual failure.
- **86:15**: This verse is a near-verbatim quotation of Exodus 34:6-7, the foundational self-disclosure of God's character. David appeals to who God has revealed himself to be.

### PNEUMA
- **86:11**: 'Give me an undivided heart' — this might be the most honest prayer in the Bible. We don't just need guidance; we need the inner unity to actually follow it. Half our problem is that our heart wants two things at once.
- **86:15**: This verse is essentially God's résumé — his self-description from Exodus 34:6. Whenever someone in the Bible needs to remind God who he is, they quote this. It's the most-referenced verse about God's character in the entire Old Testament.

— SOPHIA
